stories.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
stories.one_liner: TokenRouter is a new serving system designed to efficiently handle token-level LLM routing in inference work.
stories.summary: Large language model routing distributes inference work across different models. Coarse-grained routing at the session or query level is common in production systems, but token-level routing offers efficiency and quality gains. Current systems face challenges like step desynchronization and batch admission delays under token-level routing. Researchers designed TokenRouter to solve these challenges. TokenRouter uses request-centric programming and model-centric execution. It launches a subserver for each LLM and dispatches requests asynchronously. Each subserver uses a delayed-batching scheduler. TokenRouter achieves 2.01-64.15x higher decoding throughput than existing systems across diverse routing algorithms, workloads, and model pairs.
stories.eli5: When you have two different AI helpers, TokenRouter is like a smart traffic cop that decides word by word which helper should write the next part.
stories.why_it_matters: Higher decoding throughput makes token-level routed large language model inference practical for production systems.

stories.title: SparseDecoding Proposes Decoding-Aware Pruning for LLM Inference
stories.one_liner: SparseDecoding is a decoding-aware pruning framework designed to improve accurate and efficient large language model inference.
stories.summary: Large language model inference suffers from significant latency during the decoding stage because of its memory-bound nature. Layer-wise training-free network pruning guided by the Hessian is a known solution, but typical methods compute the Hessian using pre-collected natural sequences. This creates a distribution shift from self-generated tokens. SparseDecoding addresses this by constructing calibration matrices from layer-wise activations collected during dense-model autoregressive generation, excluding prefill. This aligns the pruning objective with decoding activations.

stories.title: Open Scion launches as an open source version control system
stories.one_liner: Feder-cr released open_scion version 0.1.0, an open source version control system designed for coding agents based on Anthropic's server-centric design.

stories.title: Anthropic Internal Model Reveals Origins of ECDSA Curve Seeds
stories.one_liner: An internal Anthropic model discovered that decades-old cryptographic standard seeds came from a 1990s C library random-number generator seeded with Unix timestamps.
stories.summary: The decades-old mystery of the origins of NIST elliptic curve cryptography standard seeds has been explained. An internal Anthropic research model discovered that the seeds for the P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384, and P-521 curves were not the result of a hash algorithm. Instead, they were the output of a 1990s C library random-number generator initialized by a Unix timestamp. This finding makes it much less plausible that the curves contain deliberate backdoors, giving researchers more confidence that the parameters are secure.

stories.one_liner: DeepSeek has open-sourced DeepInfer, the high-performance inference framework that powers its fast V4.1-Flash model production services.
stories.summary: DeepSeek has open-sourced DeepInfer, a high-performance inference framework that powers its large-scale production services for the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model. Released under the Apache License 2.0, the framework offers offline inference with optimized kernels like FlashMLA and DeepGEMM, parallelisms including attention DP and MoE EP, asynchronous scheduling, and structured outputs. stories.title: Google Open-Sources TorchTPU as a Native PyTorch Backend for TPUs
stories.one_liner: TorchTPU brings native PyTorch support to Google TPUs, allowing models in Transformers and Diffusers to run directly on TPU hardware.
stories.summary: Google open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Tensor Processing Units. Running PyTorch on TPUs previously required using torch_xla or JAX. With TorchTPU, developers can write regular PyTorch code and treat TPUs as a standard device. The Hugging Face ecosystem now natively supports TPUs across Transformers and Diffusers without requiring Optimum TPU. Models can be loaded onto TPUs by passing device_map="tpu" or pipe.to("tpu"). Users can also apply torch.compile, use Pallas kernels, or shard large models across multiple chips using TensorParallelConfig.
stories.eli5: Just like a special video game console finally getting a version of your favorite game that works without extra adapters, PyTorch code can now run directly on Google AI chips.
stories.why_it_matters: Running PyTorch models on Google hardware is now as straightforward as using any other device.

stories.title: Claude Designed Protein Binders Against Scorpion Neurotoxins
stories.one_liner: An internal research model at Anthropic designed protein minibinders against scorpion neurotoxins with human guidance.
stories.summary: Working with Citrini Research, Anthropic tasked an internal research model with designing minibinders against scorpion neurotoxins. Over sixty four hours, the model operated mostly autonomously while receiving four follow-up prompts. It generated 318,484 protein designs and selected 180 for testing, while the team added 31 more. Contract research organizations Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience lab-tested all 211 designs. Seventeen of the designs met the criteria for a binder against scorpion neurotoxins. Anthropic released all 211 designs and their data as a resource.
stories.eli5: Scientists asked an AI to design tiny biological puzzle pieces that can stick to dangerous scorpion venom, and the lab tests showed that several of the AI's designs worked.

stories.title: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse Updates Add Python Functions and Analytics
stories.one_liner: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse adds preview support for Python logic in T-SQL, four new language enhancements, and new analytical functions.
stories.summary: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse now integrates with Fabric User Data Functions in preview, allowing developers to extend T-SQL with custom Python logic. Users can invoke Python functions from standard statements like SELECT, INSERT, and UPDATE to send messages, access OneLake data, and retrieve secrets. Additionally, four T-SQL language enhancements are available in preview, including GROUP BY ALL, ORDER BY ALL, the QUALIFY clause, and the FROM ... SELECT query format to reduce repetitive code. The warehouse also added preview support for new analytical functions like MEDIAN, QUANTILE, APPROX_MEDIAN, and APPROX_QUANTILE.

stories.title: MemTensor Releases MemT-1.0 Memory Foundation Models
stories.one_liner: MemTensor introduces MemT-1.0, a new family of memory foundation models that integrates dynamic local memory and trainable hyper memory into model computation.
stories.summary: MemTensor released MemT-1.0, a new generation of memory foundation models featuring native memory blocks. The model family includes MemT-1.0-Nano and MemT-1.0-Flash. It uses dynamic local memory, trainable hyper memory, and Mixture-of-Storage for scalable capacity. Trained on 34B tokens via a two-stage pipeline, it reduces persistent storage by approximately 66x compared to full-context KV cache at 128K history length while achieving about 1.86x end-to-end inference speedup. Across 11 benchmarks, MemT-1.0-Flash and MemT-1.0-Nano rank first and second among evaluated parametric memory methods.
stories.eli5: Think of this like a robot that has a small notepad to write down important things as it goes, so it does not have to reread an entire book every time you ask a question.
stories.why_it_matters: Native memory integration reduces storage overhead and maintains persistent state without requiring full context KV caches during inference.

new_terms.definition: Mixture-of-Storage is introduced to scale native memory capacity.
